title: TRANSTHORACIC ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY REPORT
author: Dr. Farzana Rahman, MBBS, MD (Cardiology)
impression:
1. Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with normal LV systolic function (LVEF 58%).
2. Grade I (impaired relaxation) LV diastolic dysfunction.
3. Mild mitral regurgitation. Mildly dilated left atrium.
4. No pericardial effusion. No intracardiac clot seen.

follow_ups.text: Repeat echocardiography in 12 months or sooner if symptoms change.

notes: Dates printed day first (12/10/2026 read as 12 October 2026).

sections.heading: Indication
sections.text: Atrial fibrillation, follow-up of heart failure. Exertional breathlessness for 3 months.

sections.heading: Findings
sections.text:
Left ventricle: Normal cavity size. Concentric hypertrophy. Normal global and regional wall motion; no regional wall motion abnormality seen. LV systolic function is normal with an estimated ejection fraction of 58%. Mitral inflow shows an E/A reversal consistent with grade I diastolic dysfunction (impaired relaxation).
Left atrium: Mildly dilated.
Right ventricle: Normal size and systolic function (TAPSE 2.1 cm).
Mitral valve: Structurally normal leaflets. Mild central mitral regurgitation.
Aortic valve: Trileaflet, mildly thickened, opens well. No aortic stenosis or regurgitation.
Tricuspid valve: Trace tricuspid regurgitation. Estimated PASP 29 mmHg.
Pulmonary valve: Normal.
Pericardium: No pericardial effusion.
IVC: Normal size with more than 50% inspiratory collapse.
No intracardiac mass or thrombus seen; the left atrial appendage is not well seen on transthoracic imaging.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.text:
1. Concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with normal LV systolic function (LVEF 58%).
2. Grade I (impaired relaxation) LV diastolic dysfunction.
3. Mild mitral regurgitation. Mildly dilated left atrium.
4. No pericardial effusion. No intracardiac clot seen.

sections.heading: Recommendation
sections.text: Clinical correlation. Optimise blood pressure control. Repeat echocardiography in 12 months or sooner if symptoms change.
